name: Tillandsia

project_scope.selection_mode: Two-species genus lesson from live Master Plant Pool plus existing Bromeliaceae family module
project_scope.admission_note: Both taxa are live source-pool members. This lesson does not install taxa or change taxonomy/range decisions.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Start with the gray-silver leaf surface and epiphytic habit, then zoom in for the dense peltate absorptive trichomes. Confirm Tillandsia with entire leaf margins and the bromeliad 3-sepal + 3-petal flower plan; capsules release seeds with a basal white plumose appendage.
shared_genus_characters.vegetative: Epiphytic bromeliads with simple entire leaves densely covered by absorptive peltate scales; roots function mainly for attachment in these atmospheric species.
shared_genus_characters.reproductive: Bisexual flowers with the bromeliad 3+3 perianth plan; superior ovary in the project Tillandsia doorway; fruit a capsule with plumose-comose seeds.

species_comparison_matrix.habit: Compact, tufted to ball-like clumps attached to branches, wires, or other supports; shoots are short rather than forming long hanging chains.
species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Short, narrow, strongly recurved gray-scaled leaves create the characteristic compact clump.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: A discrete compact ball/tuft with short recurved leaves points strongly toward T. recurvata in this two-species project set.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Do not infer parasitism from its position on a host tree.

species_comparison_matrix.habit: Long pendent festoons made of repeatedly branching, slender hanging stems rather than compact balls.
species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Very narrow gray-scaled leaves occur along the elongate hanging shoots.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: Long draping chains/festoons rather than discrete ball-like tufts separate T. usneoides quickly from T. recurvata.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: A small broken fragment can lose the obvious festoon silhouette; use stem architecture and repeated elongate branching rather than one leaf.

decision_sequence: Confirm an epiphytic gray-scaled bromeliad rather than lichen, moss, or a parasitic mistletoe.
Find the peltate absorptive scales and entire narrow leaves; flowers/capsules can confirm the Tillandsia doorway.
Compact discrete tuft or ball with short recurved leaves → T. recurvata.
Long pendent repeatedly branching festoon → T. usneoides.
If only a tiny fragment is present, avoid forcing species from color or one leaf; obtain a wider architecture view.
overlap_and_cautions: Both species are gray-silver because of dense absorptive trichomes, so color is not a species separator.
Both are epiphytes and may share host trees; host identity is not diagnostic.
Neither is a tree parasite in the mistletoe sense; they use supports while absorbing water and nutrients primarily from the atmosphere.
Fragmentary material can erase the strongest architecture character.

realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Mistletoes are green woody hemiparasitic plants connected physiologically to host branches; project Tillandsia are gray-scaled nonwoody epiphytes with peltate absorptive trichomes.

realistic_lookalikes.lookalike: lichens and true mosses on bark
realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Tillandsia has discrete vascular leaves and stems and eventually bromeliad flowers/capsules; lichens lack leaves/stems and moss leaves are tiny nonvascular structures without bromeliad trichomes.
Hechtia is a terrestrial/lithophytic spinose rosette with separate male/female plants; project Tillandsia are epiphytic, entire-margined, and bisexual-flowered.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Teach the fastest and strongest field split.
Make the genus/family recognition character visible instead of teaching only silhouette.
Teach epiphyte versus parasite and preserve the species architecture context.
Connect field habit to reproductive genus confirmation.

labels: do not ID from gray color alone
diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Prevent overconfident species calls when the best character is absent.

media_routing.existing_project_media: Reuse exact project/user/Joey Tillandsia material when it clearly shows whole-plant architecture or trichome detail.
media_routing.instruction: Highest-value acquisition is one same-scale ballmoss-versus-Spanish-moss architecture card plus a true trichome macro; generic host-tree glamour shots are secondary.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: If fragmentary material cannot be separated by shoot architecture, Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review should verify finer floral/vegetative characters rather than this lane performing an exhaustive review.
Species taxonomy/range certification and canonical installation remain outside this genus lesson lane.

sources.supports: Tillandsia recognition, two-species silhouette comparison, trichome and reproductive teaching
